title: Woven rollout patterns for LLM routing - notes
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a working notebook exploring a "woven" approach to cross-functional rollouts for LLM features. The idea: treat traffic routing, canaries, and A/B experiments as interlaced threads (policy + human gates + telemetry) rather than separate linear stages. Focus is on medium-risk LLM changes (model variant swaps, rerankers, safety filter adjustments) where both latency and semantic regression matter.

Audience:
- Product PMs running staged experiments
- Platform engineers owning route orchestration
- SRE/oncall who will respond to degradation signals
- Solutions engineers coordinating customer-facing private deployments

High-level pattern summary (one-liner):
- Route-level policy + microcandidates + steward dyads + progressive orthogonal slices.
- Purpose: minimize blast radius while preserving signal for quality and cost.

Pattern components (informal):
1) Microcandidate bundles
   - Instead of single model variant canaries, deploy small bundles of variants (A1, A2, B1) with constrained traffic and deterministic fallback paths.
   - Rationale: preserves ability to compare multiple axes (cost/latency/quality) without repeated releases.

2) Traffic braid (orthogonal slicing)
   - Split by independent dimensions: georegion, device class, user cohort (new vs returning), query-length bucket.
   - For each dimension keep at least one orthogonal control slice that is reserved for higher fidelity checks (no synthetic traffic).

3) Stewardship dyads
   - Assign two stewards per rollout: product steward (feature owner) + operational steward (platform/sre).
   - Responsibilities: runbooks, decision authority, immediate rollback owner.

4) Sociotechnical runway checks
   - Before any traffic lift, ensure a human-preset safety runway: preflight checklist run by stewards (see checklist section).
   - Include a “communication backstop” contact list for impacted teams and customers.

5) Telemetry and signal grammar
   - Signals grouped by class: latency (P50/P95/P99), errors, quality (eval metrics, BLEU/ROUGE-type proxies for specific tasks), hallucination proxies (off-domain triggers), business KPIs (conversion, CTR), and cost (tokens/second).
   - For LLMs, add semantic drift probes (small curated prompt set) and model-consistency checks (same prompt across variants).

Runbook skeleton (quick checklist):
- Pre-deploy
  - Confirm model artifact versioning and compatibility (kv-cache schema, tokenizer).
  - Register microcandidate bundles in routing manifest.
  - Synthetics: run 2k synthetic queries across slices, verify no hard errors and acceptable latency delta (< 15% p95).
  - Create telemetry dashboards and alert thresholds (see signals below).
  - Stakeholder ping: oncall, product, security, legal (if safety-sensitive).

- Activation (0 -> 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100% cadence)
  - 0 -> 1%: short-lived (30–60m) smoke run, human-in-loop validation of drift probes.
  - 1% -> 5%: observe for 4–24h depending on traffic velocity; keep synthetic probes every 15m.
  - 5% -> 20%: validate business KPIs and latency cost tradeoff for rolling windows.
  - 20% -> 100%: only with explicit go/no-go from stewards and if no critical alerts.

- Rollback rules (fast/slow):
  - Fast rollback: triggered by hard errors (5xx spike, p99 latency > 2x baseline, synthetic zero-shot failure) — execute automatic circuit breaker to fallback model within 1 min.
  - Slow rollback: triggered by quality regressions (semantic probe drop > X%, business KPI degradation for 6h) — steward review + staged revert.

Signal thresholds (example values — tune per product):
- p50 latency delta > 25ms or p95 delta > 100ms -> INFO alert
- error rate (5xx) > baseline + 0.5% absolute -> P1 page
- semantic-probe pass rate drop > 5% absolute -> P1 warn + paging to product
- customer-facing KPI drop (conversion/CTR) > 2% relative over 24h -> review

Observability playbook (what to look at):
- Canary diff tables: per-prompt tokenization, output-length, model-churn (top-k token probability shifts).
- Telemetry span: show per-route latency with heatmap for sequence length buckets.
- Drift probe log: when a prompt fails, include model output + scoring rubric + breadcrumb links to prompt history.

Experiment design notes (A/B hybrids):
- Hybrid A/B: run a traditional A/B for customer-facing KPI, but map each variant to microcandidate bundles to simultaneously collect low-level model signals.
- Cross-over guard: avoid cross-exposure for long-tail user flows that can bias KPI measurement (e.g., multistep flows should be sticky to variant).

Safety and compliance considerations:
- For regulated customers (Private deployments), require an explicit customer-facing rollback SLA and a pre-approved fallback policy.
- Data residency: ensure synthetic probes and telemetry exports respect PII masking and region constraints.

Communication templates (quick):
- Pager message: "Rollout X: P99 latency breach observed on route /chat/predict — auto-fallback executed to model vX-std. Action: stewards investigating; reverting traffic to baseline."
- Stakeholder update: short bulleted summary, timeline, and next steps; include link to incident doc + playback meeting slot.

Open questions / experiments to run (todo):
- How many microcandidates are optimal before costs/observability become noisy? (run factorial sims)
- Can we automate steward prompts (stewardship bot) for repetitive preflight checks without losing human judgment?
- Best ways to compute hallucination proxies at scale without human labeling? (semi-supervised heuristics?)
- Optimal slice cardinality: is 4x orthogonal slices usually enough? test with synthetic traffic variety.

Short lab plan (next 6 weeks):
- Week 1: prototype routing manifest format for microcandidate bundles (platform).
- Week 2: implement synthetic probe harness and runner (applied-ml + infra).
- Week 3: instrument dashboards and create canary-diff visualizations (observability).
- Week 4: pilot on internal non-customer feature (low risk), run 72h observation.
- Week 5: review pilot, tune thresholds, write runbook.
- Week 6: small external pilot with 2 customers under SSO/Private mode.

Notes to self (scratchpad):
- Link to earlier "stewardship" docs: CONFLUENCE-1234 (need to consolidate).
- Try renaming "canary" to "microcandidate" in UX to reduce psychological rollback friction.
- Keep examples short in dashboard to avoid alert fatigue.

References and inspiration:

- academic: "progressive exposure for ML systems" (paper draft saved in Research drive)
